newsitem.title: UK: ISO sees raw sugar prices falling to 10 cents/lb.
newsitem.headline: ISO sees raw sugar prices falling to 10 cents/lb.

text.p: The outlook for world sugar prices is likely to remain bearish as key importers fail to emerge amid the background of a global statistical surplus, the International Sugar Organization (ISO) said on Tuesday.
"There will surely be further falls in both white and raw prices and we continue to believe that they will settle at 12.5 and 10 cents/lb respectively," the ISO said in its January market report.

"It is, in our view, not a matter of if, but when." It added that while there was no evidence of increased imports by major players despite the recent lower prices, countries with poor crops such as Pakistan, Bangladesh and Indonesia would still increase their sugar imports.
But with a combined surplus of around eight million tonnes accumulated over 1995/96 and 1996/97, the fundamental situation remained unremittingly bearish, it said.
